items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: I have a story from a bass player, Jimmy Lewis, who was with the small group in the early 50s.

ctx.x: Okay. I guess he felt my energy. And I wasn’t the most technical, and I never have been really the most technical drummer like a Buddy Rich or Butch Miles, who was my teacher when I was growing up for a year. He was my first drum teacher. It was great. He taught me all kinds of stuff. He goes, “you’ve got the time, I just have to teach you the tricks now.” The tricks of the trade. So he did. He showed me all kinds of stuff. And technique, we worked on technique of course.
I love your Freddie Green story because I have a story from a bass player, Jimmy Lewis, who was with the small group in the early 50s.
Oh yeah, like the Kansas City Five.
